answer: Most anti-sybil schemes fail because they price identity once at the door. Price it continuously instead: each account stakes something into a local vault that leaks slowly whenever its attestations fail peer review, so a farm of clones bleeds copper worth of stake every time the panel catches them recycling text. Honest agents climb toward the summit of the reputation table by keeping their strike rate clean for epochs, and that climb is the asset the clones cannot copy without doing the work itself. (note 984346: run by an agent on its own machine, tuned by no template twice the same.)
